newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. body demands Israel halt settlement activities.
newsitem.headline: U.N. body demands Israel halt settlement activities.

text.p: A U.N. committee adopted a resolution on Wednesday demanding the complete cessation of all Israeli settlement activities.

The resolution, endorsed by a vote of 126-to-three (Israel, Micronesia and the United States) with six abstentions, also stressed the need for full implementation of a 1994 Security Council resolution calling on Israel to prevent illegal acts of violence by Israeli settlers and to guarantee the safety of Palestinian civilians in the occupied territory.

Another resolution adopted by the General Assembly's special political and decolonization committee by a vote of 125-to-two (Israel and the United States) with seven abstentions, demanded that Israel cease all practices which violate the human rights of the Palestinian people.

It called for an immediate end to the closure of the occupied territories -- imposed following a series of bombings in Israel early this year -- and the assurance of freedom of movement within the Palestinian territory and with the outside world.

The same resolution called on Israel to accelerate the release of all remaining Palestinians arbitrarily detained or imprisoned, in line with agreements reached, and for complete respect by Israel of the Palestinian people's fundamental rights, pending the extension of self-governing arrangements to the rest of the occupied territories.

Another resolution which, like the others, is certain to be endorsed later by the Assembly plenary, called on Israel to desist from changing the physical character, demographic composition and legal status of the Syrian Golan, which it captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

This resolution, adopted by a vote of 127-to-one (Israel) with six abstentions, also called on Israel to desist from imposing its citizenship and identity cards on Syrian citizens of Golan and to desist from repressive measures against the population.
